apiDescriptions./ctp: CTP stands for Contoso Theme Parks, a fictional theme park company where a little wonder awaits every visitor. Discover Starlight Gardens and its Cloud Cruiser ride, check sample wait times, and explore a ride reservation from creation to cancellation. These static MockAPI examples do not store reservations or provide live availability; request bodies and query strings are ignored. Clearly labeled demo-faults routes demonstrate HTTP and connection failures.

endpoints.name: Discover the parks
endpoints.description: Welcome to Contoso Theme Parks! Discover the fictional Starlight Gardens park and its Cloud Cruiser attraction through a static 200 OK JSON response with an X-Mock-Source header. HEAD returns the same status and headers without a body.

endpoints.name: Explore Cloud Cruiser
endpoints.description: Discover Cloud Cruiser in Starlight Gardens' Skyward Summit land. Returns static ride details with 200 OK, including its park ID, operating status, minimum height, and a link to sample wait times. No live ride, weather, or maintenance data is queried.

endpoints.name: Reserve a ride
endpoints.description: Make room for a little adventure! Simulates a Cloud Cruiser reservation for two visitors with 201 Created and Location: /ctp/reservations/42. The request body is ignored and every call returns the same sample reservation; nothing is stored or changed.

endpoints.name: View your ride reservation
endpoints.description: Returns sample reservation 42 for Cloud Cruiser with 200 OK. This is the destination of the creation response's Location header. The fixture is always available, even before creation or after cancellation; it is not a stored reservation.

endpoints.name: Check Cloud Cruiser wait times
endpoints.description: Check a sample 15-minute wait for Cloud Cruiser. Up to four requests in a rolling 10-second window return 200 OK; additional requests return 429 Too Many Requests with a themed JSON error and Retry-After: 10. The wait time is static, not live. The dashboard preselects five requests to demonstrate the limit, and both responses include repeated X-Mock-Source header values.

response.body: {"error":"wait_times_rate_limited","message":"Take a little breather! Check back in 10 seconds."}

endpoints.name: Cancel your ride reservation
endpoints.description: Plans change, and more adventures await. Simulates cancellation of reservation 42 with 204 No Content and an empty body. Nothing is deleted; repeated cancellations return the same response and GET /ctp/reservations/42 still returns the sample reservation.

endpoints.name: Find the featured attraction
endpoints.description: Follow today's spotlight to Cloud Cruiser. Returns 302 Found with Location: /ctp/attractions/cloud-cruiser and an empty body. Clients that follow redirects receive the ride's static 200 OK JSON details.

endpoints.name: Parade schedule fault demo
endpoints.description: Intentional HTTP failure demo: the fictional parade schedule service always returns 500 Internal Server Error with a themed JSON error. Use it to test client error handling; it does not cause a real application error or represent live park operations.

response.body: {"error":"parade_schedule_unavailable","message":"The parade schedule hit a little hiccup. Please try again later."}

endpoints.name: Ride sensor connection fault demo
endpoints.description: Intentional transport failure demo: the fictional Cloud Cruiser sensor connection is immediately aborted without an HTTP status, headers, or body. Test network-failure handling separately from HTTP errors. No real ride sensors or safety systems are involved.
